resources.string: Fast file transfer between two phones over Wi-Fi Direct. No internet or mobile data needed.
Permission needed to find nearby devices
Wi-Fi is off. Turn it on (it does not need to be connected to a network).
Location is off. Android needs it to find nearby devices.

1. On the receiving phone open “Receive files” first.
2. On the sending phone open “Send files”, search, and tap the receiving phone. Accept the invitation on the receiving phone.
3. Choose any number of files of any type, or share them straight from Gallery or Files with “Send with WifiP2P”.
4. Keep both phones close (a few metres) with both screens on. Phones with Android 10+ use the fast 5 GHz band automatically.
5. Received files are saved in Downloads/WifiP2P.

To find and connect to nearby phones Android requires the “Nearby devices” (or Location) permission. The app never reads your location. On Android 9 and older it also needs storage access to save the received files.
